description: Which backends support which features, at what level, with what evidence. This is the table the website presents and the table a runtime consults before claiming compatibility.

statuses.stable: Implemented and covered by the named evidence. A mismatch between this table and a test is a bug in one of the two.
statuses.partial: Implemented for a subset. The subset is named in `limitations`.
statuses.experimental: Present but not claimed. A runtime or verifier must not advertise it as supported.
statuses.unsupported: Not implemented. Must fail loudly, never silently fall back.

evidence_policy.rule: Every non-unsupported cell names an evidence path in this repository. A cell with no evidence is downgraded to experimental. The website copies this file; it does not restate it in prose, because two hand-maintained tables drift.

evaluator.description: Tree-walking evaluator. REPL and development path.

tasks_futures.limitations: Same cancellation gaps as the VM: no explicit cancellation, and a faulting child surfaces as cancellation rather than as its cause. The evaluator pre-scans for capabilities and so also does not gate indirect calls.

capability_gate.limitations: A pre-scan that sees direct calls only, running before evaluation. It cannot report a refusal site and it does not gate indirect calls. The VM path is the enforced one.

vm.description: Bytecode compiler plus VM. The enforced execution path.

gc.limitations: Task and future roots, child-VM heap inheritance and periodic root refresh are implemented and unit covered. Long-running stress and race scenarios are not yet a CI gate.

tasks_futures.limitations: Fulfilled, Faulted and time-driven cancellation are implemented and asserted clause by clause against docs/spec/CONCURRENCY.md. Two gaps: (1) explicit cancellation is not implemented — there is no cancel() in the language, so the cascading-cancellation rules in §3.1 have no way to be triggered, a timeout is the only route to a cancelled tree, and siblings cannot be cancelled; (2) when a child task faults, the parent surfaces TaskCancelled rather than naming the child's cause, so a fault two tasks deep is indistinguishable from a timeout.

capability_gate.limitations: Direct statically named calls are gated at the call site. Indirect calls through a function value are not gated, and the `requires` clause with E0201 does not exist.

native_op_dispatch.limitations: OpNativeCall is emitted for every operation in the requirement table. An operation with no implementation is an error rather than a silent null, but the set of implemented natives is smaller than the set of gated ones.

ffi.limitations: Declaration and library-flag resolution are covered. Linking is proven on a subset of targets only.

dap.limitations: Process-level sessions are covered with generous timeouts; timeout and breakpoint behaviour is not characterised.

fmt_check.evidence: CI dx-gate job, nil fmt --check over examples, std and bootstrap

mir.description: HIR to MIR lowering into the VM.

language_core.limitations: Parity is asserted for the tested corpus only. A construct absent from that corpus is unproven, not working.

scope_shadowing.evidence: tests/scope_corpus_test.go — per-pass loop bindings and shadowed lets agree across backends including AOT.

typed_hir.limitations: Typed HIR is the input; it is not yet the only input.

ssa_cfg_optimizer.limitations: Optimized and unoptimized output parity is required but the optimizer is not enabled everywhere, so the requirement is only partially discharged.

language_core.limitations: Scope handling is covered; broad feature coverage is not.

ffi.limitations: Library flag resolution is covered; linking on every supported target is not proven.

gpu_real_submit.limitations: The GPU path is a simulation.

reproducibility.limitations: Byte-identical output is proven for bundles built from the VM path.

language_core.limitations: Some builtins are unimplemented in compiler/wasm.
Not conformance tested against the canonical backends.

cross_repo_claims.rule: A Rust mini-VM in onuronOS is a subset runtime, not a second implementation of the language. It may claim support only for the subset its conformance run covers. Any construct it cannot execute must be refused explicitly, not approximated.

The emulator installs and runs artifacts produced by the canonical compiler. Its own VM does not re-derive language semantics. QEMU is authoritative for hardware behaviour; the desktop simulator is not a second language runtime.
Alap's own parser, compiler, stdlib and VM are not a language conformance reference. Its compiler path must delegate to, or track, the canonical one.
The store presents this file. It does not author it. A store entry whose maturity is higher than its owner repo's claim is a defect in the store.
